official_name: Mental Disorders Due to Another Medical Condition
plain_title: When a physical illness is the cause of mental symptoms
one_liner: Mood, anxiety, psychosis, or personality changes that are directly caused by a medical illness, not a primary mental disorder.
in_simple_words: Sometimes a physical illness is the direct cause of mental symptoms: a thyroid problem causing depression or anxiety, a brain tumour or epilepsy causing personality change, lupus or an infection causing psychosis, or a head injury changing behaviour. The DSM labels these 'due to another medical condition' because treating the medical cause is the key. They're easy to miss. Clues include an unusual age of onset, no family history, or new physical problems.
what_it_can_feel_like: Two years of 'treatment-resistant depression' turned out to be an underactive thyroid. One blood test.
Dad's personality changed completely at 58. Everyone said midlife crisis. It was a frontal lobe tumour, and surgery gave him back to us.
common_signs: Mental symptoms that start alongside, or soon after, a physical illness
Unusual pattern: first episode late in life, no family history, or odd features
Physical signs the usual condition doesn't explain
Symptoms that improve when the medical condition is treated

myths_vs_facts.fact: Thyroid, hormone, autoimmune, neurological, and infectious conditions can all cause them. Good psychiatry starts with a medical check.

myths_vs_facts.myth: If a scan or blood test is normal, it's all in your head.
myths_vs_facts.fact: Normal tests rule some causes out, not all. And a primary mental disorder is just as real and treatable as a medical one.

how_common.plain: Overall numbers aren't known because these conditions are counted under each medical cause. They're common in hospital settings, especially among older adults.
how_common.figure: No overall prevalence figure; varies by underlying condition

what_helps.plain_summary: Treatment targets the medical cause first: correcting the thyroid, treating the infection or autoimmune disease, managing the epilepsy, removing the tumour. Mental symptoms often ease as the condition improves. In the meantime, the usual treatments for mood, anxiety, or psychosis are used with care, prescribed and monitored by a doctor who knows the medical picture. Psychiatry, neurology, and general medicine often work together.
evidence_based_options: Full medical assessment including blood tests and, where indicated, brain imaging
Treatment of the underlying medical condition
Psychiatric treatment of the symptoms meanwhile, adjusted for the medical condition
Joint care between psychiatry and medical specialists
self_help_that_supports_care: Asking for a physical check-up when mental symptoms are new or unusual
Listing all medications and supplements for the doctor
Noting the timeline: what started when
Bringing a family member who's noticed changes

when_to_reach_out: If mental symptoms have started suddenly, late in life, alongside physical changes, or don't respond to usual treatment, ask for a medical review. If someone becomes confused or behaves very differently over hours or days, seek urgent care.
is_not: Being understandably upset about having an illness isn't a disorder due to that illness. Delirium and dementia have their own cards. Depression that happens to coexist with a medical condition, without being caused by it, is diagnosed as depression.
hope_note: When the cause is found and treated, symptoms that seemed stubborn often lift. It's one reason a medical check is always worth it.
